name: Music Ducking With Volume Keyframes
use_when: A single music bed should be louder under montage, product, travel, or B-roll sections and lower under speech.
The edit alternates between no-dialogue visual clips and talking sections.
The editor needs simple CapCut-style volume automation rather than a full audio mix.
avoid_when: The music track is unlicensed, unsafe, or only a temporary reference.
The music tone fights the speaker, subject, or story.
Dialogue needs cleanup, gain repair, or a better source before music is added.
A hard music cut or different track would serve the section better than constant up/down automation.

timeline_pattern.pre_duck_rule: Place the duck keyframe before speech starts so the first word is clear.
timeline_pattern.restore_rule: Restore music only after the phrase, thought, or speech section clears.
timeline_pattern.section_rule: Use louder music under visual-only sections and lower music under dialogue; do not automate constantly without a section reason.
timeline_pattern.license_rule: Document whether the music is licensed, platform-safe, temp-only, or unsafe before delivery.

motion.rule: Music rises can support visual montage or product clips, but should not force unrelated visual cuts.

sound.rule: Speech remains dominant during talking sections.

keyframe_values.capcut_duck_start: In CapCut, dropping music volume near 1-2 can be an effective starting point under speech, then adjust by ear.
keyframe_values.db_range: As a starting range, music under speech often lands around -15 dB to -20 dB; a softer bed may work around -14 dB if every word remains clear.
keyframe_values.restore_to_full: When the talking section ends, return music toward full level or 0 dB over a few frames only after the phrase clears.
keyframe_values.duck_timing: Start ducking before the first spoken word and restore after the dialogue phrase ends.
keyframe_values.preview: Preview on phone speakers because music that sounds low in headphones may still mask speech on mobile.

captions.rule: Captions can support speech but do not excuse music that masks normal dialogue.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use volume envelopes, afade, sidechaincompress where appropriate, and waveform/loudness review around speech starts.
implementation.remotion: Store audio gain keyframes for music with duckStartFrame, lowGain, restoreFrame, and dialogueRanges.
implementation.blender: Use VSE audio-strip volume keyframes and preview speech sections after restoring music.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Select the music track, add full-volume keyframes for montage sections, add pre-duck and low-volume keyframes under speech, then restore to full volume after talking clears.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use clip volume rubber-band keyframes or Essential Sound ducking; manually check that ducks begin before speech and restore after phrases.

common_mistakes: Starting the duck after the first spoken word has already been masked.
Restoring music too early under the end of a sentence.
Using one numeric duck value for every track instead of checking the actual song against the voice.
Using music that is unsafe or unlicensed because it was easy to import.
Leaving music loud enough that captions become necessary for normal speech.
Automating volume constantly without clear montage/speech sections.
qc: Is the music licensed, platform-safe, or clearly marked temp-only?
Does music duck before the first spoken word?
Is dialogue intelligible without needing captions as rescue?
Does the music restore only after speech clears?
Are the loud montage sections energetic without clipping or overpowering SFX?
